chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
A man should have the hair removed (be shaved) on Wednesday, for it is a continuously unlucky day.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of shaving on Wednesday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) advises men to shave on Wednesdays, linking the act to the day's reputation for continuous misfortune (*nahs*). This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of *takhassus* (specialization) in daily rituals, where specific days are associated with particular spiritual or physical states, encouraging believers to align their hygiene practices with cosmic rhythms to ward off ill omens.
